items.title: Winard Harper interviewed by Monk Rowe, Utica, New York, October 10, 2014
items.q: You know Art Blakey was still around... Most of us pretty much had like a four year run with her. And the same thing with a lot of guys that worked with Art Blakey and the Jazz Messengers

ctx.x: Well what were the opportunities that were there before that aren’t here now?

Well I think one, first off, there were more venues. There were more places to play. When we came along I could at least say maybe in almost every major city there was at least one club or place that you could hope to play and work. It’s not quite that way today. And then on top of that what a lot of us that came along let’s say late 70s, 80s, there were some bands you could play in. You could go apprentice with somebody. You know Art Blakey was still around; Betty Carter; Horace Silver, that band; Sonny Rollins.…
Yeah, to keep the same group of people together. And you did that.
